subject: SIG: Clarify prompt/log retention & training on customer data
messages:
From: Gina Lee <gina.lee@velorahealth.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: security@velorahealth.com
Date: 2026-06-29T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: SIG follow-up: prompt/log retention and training on customer data

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the quick intro earlier. As we work through the SIG questionnaire I have a couple of follow-ups specific to data handling that we need written confirmation for:

1) Prompt and transient logs: what is Redwood's default retention period for request/response logs and KV/prefix caches? Do you make any copies for backend analytics?

2) Training on customer data: do you use customer prompts or generated outputs to further train models or fine-tune weights? If not, can you provide an explicit commitment and any contractual language we can reference?

3) Redaction and evidence: can you provide a redacted sample prompt/log entry and a short diagram showing where ephemeral caches live (customer-only RAM, Redis, disk?), plus the retention enforcement point?

4) Exceptions: are there any circumstances (legal, security, or ops troubleshooting) where logs are retained longer? If so, what controls and approvals exist?

Can you get us a short, document-ready response and the sample artifacts by EOD tomorrow? Attach the SIG workbook if helpful.

Appreciate it — Gina
Velora Health — Security Engineering

Attachments: Velora_SIG_Questions_v2.xlsx (attached)

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Gina Lee <gina.lee@velorahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: prompt/log retention and training on customer data

Gina —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick summary up front, then attached artifacts and a redacted sample. Full details below and in the attached SIG_response_Redwood_20260629.docx and redwood_retention_policy_2026.pdf.

Short answers:
- Default prompt/request logs: retained for 7 days (ephemeral logs used for routing/diagnostics).
- KV/prefix cache: in-memory only per-instance; persistent checkpoints are not retained across customer sessions unless explicitly enabled by the customer (see doc).
- Training on customer data: Redwood does NOT use customer prompt/response content to train or fine-tune public models by default. We only use telemetry/metrics (anonymized token-level stats) for product improvements. Any use of customer content for training requires explicit written opt-in at the account level.
- Exceptions: legal hold or incident investigation may require extended retention; such requests go through our Security & Legal teams and are logged with approval timestamps.

Attachments: SIG_response_Redwood_20260629.docx (formal answers), redwood_retention_policy_2026.pdf (policy), architecture_kv_cache_diagram.png (high-level diagram).

Full detail (for the SIG workbook):
1) Retention windows
  - Request/response logs (engine debug logs with content): default retention 7 days. Logs are stored encrypted at rest while retained.
  - Aggregated telemetry (usage counters, latency histograms): retained for 25 months for product analytics.
  - KV/prefix cache: primarily in-memory per server; we persist snapshots only when customers enable stateful sessions (explicit feature) and those snapshots are retained per the customer's configured retention policy.

2) Training and model updates
  - We do not train models on customer prompt/response content without opt-in. Engineering and research teams operate on synthetic or internally curated datasets.
  - If a customer opts in, the opt-in is scoped, timeboxed, and reversible; all training datasets are logged and subject to access controls.

3) Redaction and sample artifacts
  - Attached is a redacted prompt/log sample (redacted_sample_prompt_log_20260629.json) showing token masking.
  - The architecture diagram highlights that ephemeral caches live in-process or in a per-customer Redis with TTL enforcement; retention enforcement happens at the storage layer and is audited.

4) Exceptions and approvals
  - Legal holds are handled by our Security & Legal teams; retention is extended only after documented approval, and we provide audit entries to customers on request.

I'll loop in Vanessa to provide a short contract-style statement you can paste into the SIG workbook and to attach the redacted sample.

— Alex
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Alex — thanks, that helps a lot. A couple quick clarifications before we mark the SIG as answered: 

- The 7 day default: does that apply to both request/response payloads and any raw debug traces that might include full prompts?
- For aggregated telemetry retained 25 months, can you confirm that those artifacts never contain unhashed prompt text or outputs (only token counts/latency/error codes)?
- For legal hold processes, do you provide customers a copy of the approval/log that triggered extended retention? We need that for our auditors.

If you can provide one short, contract-ready sentence we can paste into the SIG and a redacted log sample (even just one entry) that shows the masking approach, we should be able to close this out.

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: prompt/log retention and training on customer data

Hi Gina —

Apologies for the brief delay — attaching a redacted single-entry sample and the formal, contract-friendly statement below that you can paste into the SIG workbook. The attached sample (redacted_sample_prompt_log_20260629.json) demonstrates our masking: PII and user identifiers are replaced with stable hashes; prompt/output text is replaced with a token-summary when retained beyond 24 hours.

Contract-ready statement (paste into SIG):
"Redwood Inference retains full request/response payloads for up to seven (7) days by default to support routing, diagnostics, and short-term troubleshooting. Aggregated usage telemetry (metrics, counters, latency histograms) is retained for up to twenty-five (25) months and does not contain raw prompt or output text. Redwood does not use customer-provided prompts or generated outputs to train or fine-tune production models without explicit, documented customer opt-in; any exceptional retention for legal hold or incident response is approved by Redwood Security & Legal and is recorded in audit logs that can be shared with the customer upon request."

Additional notes: 
- Yes, the 7-day default applies to request/response payloads and raw debug traces that contain customer-provided text.
- Aggregated telemetry is token-counts and error codes only; it does not contain raw or unhashed prompt text.
- For legal holds we provide the customer a copy of the retention approval and associated audit log entries; we can include that in an evidence package if needed.

Let us know if you'd like a short notarized statement or an SLA appendix; happy to coordinate with Legal.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference
